title: Min-Max Range Stack
description:
Design a stack `RangeStack` that supports standard stack operations plus retrieving the value range (`max - min`) of all elements currently in the stack in constant `O(1)` time.

Implement the `RangeStack` class:
- `RangeStack()` initializes an empty stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes the 32-bit signed integer `val` onto the stack.
- `void pop()` removes the top element of the stack.
- `int top()` returns the top element of the stack.
- `long getRange()` returns `(long) maxVal - (long) minVal` across all elements currently in the stack.

Every operation must run in `O(1)` time.
constraints: Methods pop, top, and getRange are always called on non-empty stacks.
At most 3 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Alongside each pushed value, store the running minimum and running maximum at that stack depth.
Compute max - min using 64-bit signed integers (long in Java) so extreme 32-bit bounds do not overflow.

examples.explanation: After pushing 4, 1, 9, range is 9 - 1 = 8; after popping 9, stack is [4, 1] with top 1 and range 4 - 1 = 3.
With a single element 7, max equals min so getRange returns 0.
